data.content_ref: inline:The target concedes the non-experts may 'reach the right answer' (via brittle compliance that tracks correctness), yet never identifies what within-evaluation evidence would distinguish that mere-compliance case from a genuine reliability gain — the exact second task the problem demands. Its only observation-type counterconditions address when brittle compliance won't occur, not how to tell compliance-with-correct-answer apart from true reliability within a single evaluation.
